obverse.design: The front side of this standard Series 2013 United States $1 bill features a central portrait of George Washington. It displays a green Treasury Seal on the right and a black Federal Reserve Bank Seal on the left with the letter 'E', indicating it was issued in Richmond, Virginia. The note is printed with the green serial number E 93235816 J on a durable fabric paper blend composed of 75% cotton and 25% linen.

reverse.design: The back side of the bill focuses on national symbols, centered around the large word 'ONE' and the official motto 'In God We Trust.' It prominently features the two circular faces of the Great Seal of the United States. The left circle displays an unfinished pyramid topped by the Eye of Providence, while the right circle depicts the American bald eagle holding an olive branch and arrows.

obverse.design: The front side features a central portrait of George Washington, the first President of the United States. This specific note belongs to Series 2001 and is signed by Treasurer Rosario Marin and Secretary of the Treasury Paul H. O'Neill. The black circular seal on the left contains a large 'G', which stands for the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, Illinois. The matching green serial number, G 26052774 B, is printed twice, framing the portrait alongside the green Department of the Treasury seal on the right.

reverse.design: The back side features the word 'ONE' prominently in the center, overlaid with the national motto 'IN GOD WE TRUST'. Flanking the text are the two sides of the Great Seal of the United States. The left circle displays an unfinished pyramid topped by the Eye of Providence, symbolizing divinity and strength. The right circle features an American bald eagle holding an olive branch and arrows, representing peace and war, beneath a constellation of 13 stars.

obverse.design: Norochcholai Coal Power Plant Project at the center, with the Laxapana waterfall in the background. It displays an endemic bird, the Sri Lankan Orange Billed Babbler (Turdoides rufescens), on the right side and an Autumn Leaf butterfly (Doleschallia bisaltidae)

obverse.design: The portrait of King Maha Vajiralongkorn (King Rama X), the current reigning monarch of Thailand, depicted in the ceremonial uniform of the Commander of the Royal Thai Air Force

reverse.design: Historical portraits of the first two Chakri dynasty monarchs: King Rama I (Phra Buddha Yodfa Chulaloke) on the left and King Rama II (Phra Buddha Loetla Nabhalai) on the right, set against a background depicting the Grand Palace in Bangkok.

obverse.design: The front of the banknote features a detailed depiction of Mount Everest (Chomolungma) on the left side and the historic Taleju Temple of Kathmandu in the center. The top prominently displays the issuer's name in Devanagari script alongside the note's face value of five rupees. A watermark window containing the national flower, the Rhododendron, sits on the right side.

reverse.design: The back of the banknote showcases two Himalayan yaks grazing with the snow-capped Himalayan mountain range stretching across the background. It features the official English lettering of the central bank, 'NEPAL RASTRA BANK,' the denomination 'RUPEES FIVE,' and the specific Gregorian calendar year marked as '2012 A.D' at the bottom center.
